sentences: Preheat oven to 180C/350F.
Melt 1 tbsp / 20g butter in ovenproof pot (preferably with a lid) over medium high heat.
Garnish with crispy sage, 1 or 2 teaspoons of brown butter and parmesan cheese.
Toss beef in skillet with 1 cup braising liquid (aka Consomme).
Heat 1 tsp Birria oil over low heat, wipe pan with tortilla, remove, repeat x2 with 1/2 tsp oil each.
Roughly chop into 1 - 1.5cm / 1/4" pieces.
Reserve 1/2 cup of chilli-simmering water.
Birria Adobo (paste) - Place cooked chillies, reserved 1/2 cup chilli water and remaining Adobo ingredients in a tall jug large enough to fit the head of a stick blender.
Sear beef - Heat the oil in a large heavy based pot over high heat (I use my 24cm / 9.6" dutch oven).
Add the 1/2 teaspoon of salt and toss meat to distribute.
Birria oil - Skim off as much of the red oil floating on braising liquid surface as possible (ideally 6 tbsp+) and place in a separate bowl (this is the "Birria Oil").
Soak beef - Pour 1 cup of the braising liquid ("Birria Consommé") into a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat.
Red tortillas - Heat 1 teaspoon Birria Oil in the same non-stick pan over medium-low heat.
Repeat twice more, heating 1/2 teaspoon Birria Oil for each tortilla.
Beef: Place in a bowl and add 1 1/2 tbsp Sauce.
Drizzle 1 tbsp of sake onto each fish.
Bake at 180C/350F for 15 minutes.
Preheat oven to 180C°/350°F (160°C fan).
Grease a 23 x 33cm / 9 x 13" metal cake pan with butter.
(You could also use a stick blender, but a stand mixer will not work)
Spread on a shallow bowl-plate / regular plate so it's around 1.5cm / 0.6" thick.
Preheat oven to 200F/100C (for keeping fritters warm).
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a non stick pan over medium high heat (or medium if stove is strong).
Drop 1/4 cup batter in the pan (ice cream scoop is perfect).
Flatten lightly with spatula to about 1cm / 4/5" thick.
Infuse milk: Place milk, vanilla seeds, used beans and 50g (1/4 cup) sugar in a large saucepan over medium high heat.
Cut three 25 x 5.5cm  (2.15 x 10″) wide strips on the other sheet of puff pastry.
Line pan: Butter and line the sides of a 20cm/8" springform pan with a 5.5cm / 2.2" strip of baking paper.

Working quickly, when sides have JUST thawed enough to bend, line sides of cake pan with puff pastry, overlapping by 1cm / 0.4", using water to seal - just press down for now (will seal properly later).
Seal pastry: Use the back of a teaspoon to press base into the corner.
Preheat oven to 220°C/430°F (200°C fan) for 30 minutes.
Crumple 2 x 60cm / 2 feet long sheets of baking paper (Note 7) then fit into crust arranged in X.
Fill with baking beads 1cm / 0.4" below rim (Note 8).
Turn oven down to 200°C/390°F (180°C fan).
Whisk to loosen, scrape into crust - fill to 1cm/0.4" below rim.
Bake 65 minutes, rotating tray 180° at 45 minutes.
Preheat oven to 200°C / 390°F (180°C fan-forced).
Carve / cut each potato into cylinders ~ 6cm/ 2" diameter, 7 cm height.
Then cut in half so you have 8 short cylinders 3.5 cm / 1.4" tall.
Sear - In an ovenproof heavy based skillet (Note 2), heat the remaining 1 tbsp oil over medium high heat.
Once carved into a tall cylinder 6cm/ 2" diameter, at least 7cm/3" height, so we can cut into 3.5 cm / 1.4" tall pieces.
Easy - Use 6cm/ 2" (or as close as possible) wide cutters to press rounds out!
Doesn't matter! - Just cut potatoes into 3.5cm / 1.4" thick slices!
Preheat oven to 180°C / 350°F (160°C fan-forced).
Line the base of a 23 x 33cm / 13 x 9" pan with paper (Note 5)
Spread base and lid with the 1/3 cup mustard.
Preheat oven to 190°C/375°F (170°C fan).
Form 2.5cm/1" balls: Scoop up about 1 tablespoon of the mixture and shape into a rough ball (2.5cm/1" ball).
Bake 13 minutes: Place on prepared tray 2.5cm / 1" apart.
Heat 1 1/2 tbsp olive oil in a large pot over medium high heat.
Preheat oven to 180°F/350°F (160°C fan).
Add apricots, put the lid back on and cook for another 1 hour, checking halfway to ensure the sauce hasn't reduced all the way (if you're concerned, add 1/2 cup water).
Preheat oven to 220°C/425°F (200°C fan-forced).
Cut into 3cm / 1.2" squares.
Dressing - Shake the dressing ingredients in a jar until well combined.
Preheat oven to 150C/300F.
Set aside 1 1/2 tbsp of the Spice Mix for later (to pan fry the lamb).
Heat 1 tbsp of oil in a heavy based pan over high heat.
Add some lamb (don't crowd the pan) and drizzle over about 3 tbsp of the pan juices.
Just before they're done, add the garlic and a pinch of salt and pepper.
Cook in a lightly buttered non-stick pan, swirling ¼ cup batter to cover the surface.
Heat a 24cm / 9.5" non-stick crêpe pan over medium-high heat (medium if your stove runs hot).
Melt about 1/2 tsp butter, then wipe it off with a paper towel, you want just a little of butter left, no visible pools.

Pour the batter - Using a ladle, scoop up ¼ cup of batter, lift the pan off the heat, ladle most of the batter into the centre, and immediately swirl the pan so the batter coats the surface in a thin, even layer.
Preheat oven to 220C / 430F (standard oven) or 200C / 390F (fan forced / convection).
Remove tray from oven, flick to broiler/grill on high (shelf about 20cm/8" from heat source).
Preheat grill/broiler to medium high with shelf about 25cm/10" from heat source.
Spread with butter, then 1 tbsp Russian Dressing on each piece.
Chicken Marinade: Transfer 1/4 cup of Yoghurt Ranch Dressing into a bowl with the chicken.
Scatter over grapefruit, onion (not the liquid), top with a handful of snow pea sprouts, sprinkle over parmesan.
Preheat oven to 220C/430F (standard) or 200C/390F (fan / convection).
Scoop up 1 slightly heaped tablespoon and roll into a ball (about 3cm / 1.25" diameter).
Slice the white part only into 0.5cm / 1/4" slices, thick enough to pick off later if any stick to the wings.
Preheat oven to 180C/350F and put the rack in the top part of the oven.
Place Dressing ingredients in a jar and shake well to combine.
